status.down: The background monitor is not running

backendUnavailable.title: The background monitor is not responding
backendUnavailable.hint: WattScope is starting or restarting its monitor. Wait a moment and try again; if it keeps failing, see the message at the top of the window.

timeout.title: The monitor took too long to answer
timeout.hint: It may be busy. Try again in a moment.

database.title: The database could not be read or written
database.hint: Your data was not changed. Check that the disk is available and not full, then try again. The database location is shown under Settings, Diagnostics.

validation.title: That could not be done
validation.hint: The request was refused. The technical details below say why.

internal.title: Something went wrong inside WattScope
internal.hint: Try again. If it keeps happening, copy the diagnostics from Settings and include them in a bug report.

restarting.title: The background monitor stopped and is restarting
restarting.hint: WattScope restarts it automatically. The gap is recorded honestly: no energy is invented for the time it was down.

failed.title: The background monitor is not running

backend.retryFailed: The monitor could not be started again.

reason.tooManyRestarts: The monitor kept stopping unexpectedly, so automatic restarts were stopped. Nothing is being recorded. Choose Retry to start it again.
reason.recorderLockHeld: Another WattScope is already recording to this database. Close it (use Exit WattScope from its tray icon), then choose Retry.
reason.databaseError: The database could not be opened or upgraded, so nothing can be recorded. Your data was not changed. Check Diagnostics for its location, then choose Retry.
reason.spawnFailed: The monitor program could not be started. Reinstalling WattScope usually fixes this. Choose Retry to try again.

validation.currency: Enter a 3-letter currency code, for example EUR.
validation.dateTime: Enter a valid date and time.

chart.title: Live power
chart.ariaLabel: Line chart of CPU, GPU and estimated total power over the last few minutes
chart.note: A gap in a line means that reading was unavailable at that time; it is never drawn as 0 W.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: What WattScope is measuring right now.

qualityHelp.partial: CPU power is unavailable, so the system figures are lower bounds and no cost is shown. The GPU is still monitored.
qualityHelp.sensorUnavailable: No required sensor is available right now, so there is no estimate.
qualityHelp.stopped: Nothing is being recorded. Closing this window does not stop monitoring; only Stop monitoring or Exit does.
qualityHelp.unavailable: The background monitor is not running. See the message above.

hints.systemPower: Estimated system power = (CPU package + GPU board + other components) / PSU efficiency. It is calculated from sensors and two assumptions you can set; it is not read from the wall socket.
hints.otherPower: A constant you set for everything WattScope cannot measure: motherboard, memory, storage, fans. It is an assumption, not a measurement.

dashboard.approxCost: approximate, live; the exact cost is in Reports
dashboard.costWithheld: Not shown while the estimate is incomplete
dashboard.setPrice: Set an electricity price to see costs
dashboard.partialEnergyNote: Part of this session had no CPU reading. The figure above is a lower bound; {{complete}} of it is Complete energy.
dashboard.partialEnergyNoteNone: This session had no CPU reading, so none of its energy is Complete. The figure above is a lower bound.
dashboard.cpuNeedsAdmin: On some PCs the CPU sensor can only be read when WattScope is launched with Run as administrator. WattScope never elevates itself.
dashboard.monitorErrorHint: Monitoring may have stopped. You can start it again; whatever was recorded so far is kept.

gaming.title: Gaming
gaming.subtitle: Energy used while you play, measured from the same monitoring as everywhere else.
gaming.detectionOff: Automatic game detection is switched off
gaming.detectionOffHelp: Games will not be recognized automatically. You can still start a gaming session by hand.
gaming.noGameHelp: A game is recognized while monitoring is running. Launchers, browsers and other programs are not counted as games.
gaming.needsMonitoring: Monitoring is stopped. Games are only detected while WattScope is monitoring.
gaming.partialBanner: Partial: CPU power is not available, so energy and system power are lower bounds and no complete cost is shown. GPU figures are still measured.

costStatus.withheldPartial: Not shown: the estimate is partial
costStatus.withheldUnpriced: Not shown: no electricity price covers this energy

source.userMapping: Marked as a game by you
source.libraryPath: Found in a game library folder

manual.hint: For a game that is not detected automatically.
manual.help: Use this when a game is not detected automatically. The session uses the same monitoring and energy rules as an automatic one.
manual.name: Game name
manual.remember: Detect this program automatically next time

history.title: Gaming history
history.noneHelp: A session is recorded when WattScope detects a game while monitoring is running, or when you start one by hand.
history.lowerBoundNote: This session is partial: values marked with ≥ are lower bounds, not complete estimates.
history.approxPrice: * Approximate: a price was added after this session was recorded, so its cost is split by time, not by measurement.
history.limit: Showing the newest {{count}} sessions. Older ones are still included in the per-game totals below.

aggregates.title: Per game
aggregates.help: Complete and partial sessions are never added together. Averages are weighted by time, not averaged per session.

games.title: Manage games
games.help: Mark a program as a game, give it a name, or exclude it from detection. Edit or remove an entry at any time. Your choices are stored on this computer only.
games.name: Game name
games.actionsNote: Renaming applies to every session of this program. Excluding stops it from being detected as a game again; you can undo that under Manage games.
games.privacyNote: Detection only reads the list of running programs. WattScope never touches a game's memory or files and does not interact with the game.

reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: Energy and estimated cost for a day, a month or a single monitoring session. All times are your local time.
reports.invalidDate: That is not a valid date.
reports.noData: Nothing was monitored in this period. WattScope records only while monitoring is running.

hints.systemEnergy: Energy estimated for the whole PC from CPU and GPU measurements plus your assumptions. Time with every required sensor working is Complete; time with a sensor missing is Partial and is only a lower bound. The two are never added together.

reports.costNoPrice: No electricity price covered this energy
reports.partialCostNote: Partial energy would add at least
reports.unpriced: of energy was used before an electricity price existed; it is not priced, and not counted as free.
reports.gapsNote: no energy is recorded for gaps
reports.uncovered: of monitored time had no usable estimate.
reports.replayedNotice: Exact: reconstructed from raw samples recorded during this period.
reports.approxNotice: Approximate: a price was added after this period was recorded and the raw samples needed to split it exactly are no longer available.
reports.assumptionsNote: System energy = (CPU package + GPU board + other components) / PSU efficiency. Other components and PSU efficiency are assumptions, not measurements. These are the exact values used for this period:
reports.gamingOnDay: Gaming sessions that started on this day
reports.dailyNote: Complete and partial energy are shown in separate columns because they cannot be added honestly. Cost covers complete, priced energy only.
reports.noSessionsHelp: A monitoring session starts when you start monitoring. Open the Dashboard to begin.
reports.sessionsNote: Select a session number for its full report. The running session is updated every few seconds.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Changes are saved when you press Save. Each value shows its unit and the range it accepts.

monitoring.description: How often WattScope reads the sensors.
monitoring.intervalHelp: Between 250 and 60000 ms. A shorter interval follows peaks more closely; 1000 ms is a good default. Changing it continues the same session; a short gap is recorded and no energy is invented across it.

estimation.description: How WattScope turns CPU and GPU measurements into an estimate for the whole PC.
estimation.formula: Estimated system power = (CPU package power + GPU board power + other components) / PSU efficiency.
estimation.notWall: CPU and GPU power are measured by sensors. The rest is an assumption, so this is an estimate and not a measurement of wall power. A smart plug would measure that directly.
estimation.assumptionNote: An assumption you set, not a measurement.
estimation.otherWattsHelp: A constant for the parts WattScope cannot measure: motherboard, memory, storage, fans. 0 to 2000 W; 30 to 80 W is typical for a desktop.
estimation.psuHelp: How much of the power drawn from the wall reaches your components. 50 to 100 %; 85 to 92 % is typical for a modern power supply.
estimation.appliesNext: New values apply to monitoring sessions started from now on. A session that is already running, and every past session, keeps the values it was recorded with.

electricity.description: The price of electricity, used for every cost estimate. Prices are kept as a history.
electricity.none: Without a price, WattScope shows energy but no costs. Costs are never shown as zero.
electricity.priceHelp: Up to 6 decimal places, for example 0.3050. Up to 100.
electricity.currencyHelp: A 3-letter code, for example EUR. It is fixed after the first price.
electricity.fromDate: From a specific date and time
electricity.pastWarning: A date in the past changes the estimated cost of energy that is already recorded. WattScope will show you what it affects before anything is saved.
electricity.appendOnly: A new price is added to the history. Earlier prices are never edited or deleted, and the cost of past energy is only recalculated if you choose a date in the past.
electricity.historyNote: Each price applies until the next one starts. Energy is always priced at the price in effect when it was used.
electricity.confirmTitle: Apply a price to the past?
electricity.confirmBody_one: This price starts {{date}}. Energy already recorded from then on, in {{count}} monitoring session, will be re-costed at it
electricity.confirmBody_other: This price starts {{date}}. Energy already recorded from then on, in {{count}} monitoring sessions, will be re-costed at it
electricity.confirmRecalc: The new cost applies from that date until the next price change. Reports for those days will change.
electricity.confirmKept: Earlier price entries stay in the history unchanged.

data.description: What WattScope keeps on this computer, and how to look after it. Nothing here is uploaded anywhere.
data.retentionHelp: 0 to 3650 days. Only the per-second readings are pruned after this time (0 keeps none). The 15-minute energy totals, costs, sessions and gaming history are kept regardless.
data.storageNote: The database is a single local file. WattScope never deletes it automatically, and uninstalling does not remove your history by default.
data.maintenanceHelp: Removes raw samples past the retention above, returns unused space to the disk in small steps and checks the database. It never changes your totals, costs or history.
data.maintenanceDone_one: Done. {{count}} old raw sample was removed.
data.maintenanceDone_other: Done. {{count}} old raw samples were removed.
data.integrityBad: The database check found a problem
data.deleteHelp: Permanently removes finished monitoring sessions, and the gaming sessions recorded in them, that ended before the age you choose. It never touches the session that is running, your electricity prices, your settings or your game list, and it does not delete the database file.
data.deleteNothing: Nothing is that old. Nothing would be deleted.
data.deleteScope_one: {{count}} finished monitoring session would be deleted
data.deleteScope_other: {{count}} finished monitoring sessions would be deleted
data.deleteDone_one: Deleted {{count}} monitoring session and its recorded data.
data.deleteDone_other: Deleted {{count}} monitoring sessions and their recorded data.
data.confirmBody_one: {{count}} finished monitoring session will be deleted, with:
data.confirmBody_other: {{count}} finished monitoring sessions will be deleted, with:
data.confirmReports: Reports for those days and months will no longer include this energy, and costs for them will disappear.
data.confirmKept: Kept: the running session, newer history, electricity prices, estimation settings, the game list and the database file.

language.description: The language of the app and of the tray menu.
language.label: Language
language.note: Dates and numbers follow the language's conventions. Units such as W, kWh and EUR, and CPU and GPU, are always written the same way.

application.description: How WattScope runs on this computer.
application.backgroundHelp: Closing this window keeps WattScope running in the system tray and monitoring continues. WattScope only runs while you have launched it; it does not start with Windows.
application.exitHelp: Stops monitoring, saves the session and closes WattScope completely.
application.exitBody: Monitoring will stop and the current session will be saved. WattScope will not record anything until you start it again.
application.administratorHelp: On some PCs the CPU sensor can only be read when WattScope runs as Administrator. WattScope never elevates itself: for complete CPU monitoring, close it and launch it with Run as administrator.

diagnostics.failed: Diagnostics are not available right now
diagnostics.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
diagnostics.privacy: The copied text has versions, states and the two selected sensors only: no computer or user name, no database contents. The profile folder in the path is replaced by a variable.

firstRun.title: Welcome to WattScope
firstRun.intro: A quick look at what WattScope does, and what it does not know.

local.title: It stays on your PC.
local.body: WattScope monitors your computer's hardware power locally. There is no account, no cloud and no upload.

measured.title: Some values are measured.
measured.body: CPU and GPU power come straight from the sensors in your hardware.

estimated.title: The whole PC is estimated.
estimated.body: Without a smart plug, system power is calculated from those sensors plus two assumptions you can adjust. It is an estimate, not a wall measurement.

cpu.title: CPU power may need permission.
cpu.body: On some PCs it can only be read when WattScope runs as Administrator. If it is missing, WattScope says so, shows a lower bound and never guesses.

price.title: Add your electricity price for costs.
price.body: Without a price you still see energy, just no cost.

firstRun.footer: You can change all of this later in Settings.
